summary: Targeted frontend regression for VerifyQR print security fix (DOM-injection -> createElement/textContent). On the public verify page for the attested package, the VERIFIED banner renders with SHA-256 comparison, the QR dialog opens with a rendered QRCodeCanvas, and clicking 'Print verification QR' opens a popup without raising any JS/console/page errors. Popup content built via createElement+textContent is correct: title = 'PKG-2026-001 — Verify', body contains the TALA footer text, QR image has a data:image/png src. No console or page errors captured during the flow. Authenticated project-detail QR button check was not conclusive from the test harness (login succeeded 200 but app uses httpOnly cookie session; my localStorage token injection didn't authenticate the SPA and the /projects/{id} route redirected). This is a test-harness limitation, not a product bug — the shared VerifyQR component already verified safe on the public page. Main agent can self-verify authenticated QR flows via normal login UI.
critical_code_review_comments: VerifyQR.jsx print(): safe implementation — all project-supplied values (projectName, packageCode, url) are injected via textContent; only inline <style> uses textContent on static CSS and QR image uses toDataURL. No XSS surface remains.
Minor: window.open popup may be blocked by browsers; print() silently returns on null — acceptable UX but consider a toast notification if w is null.
